summary: The study reports the first atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes for HfS2 and ZrS2 using HfCl4 and ZrCl4 with H2S as precursors. The process enables the deposition of uniform and continuous films on various substrates with controlled thicknesses ranging from a few monolayers to tens of nanometers. The films are crystalline, smooth, and stoichiometric with oxygen as the main impurity. The study also demonstrates the use of a protective AlxSiyOz layer to prevent oxidation and shows the optoelectronic properties of the films through photodetector applications.
evidence: We report the first atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes for HfS2 and ZrS2 using HfCl4 and ZrCl4 with H2S as the precursors. We demonstrate the deposition of uniform and continuous films on a range of substrates with accurately controlled thicknesses ranging from a few monolayers to tens of nanometers. The use of semiconductor industry-compatible precursors and temperatures (approximately 400 °C) enables facile upscaling of the process. The deposited HfS2 and ZrS2 films are crystalline, smooth, and stoichiometric with oxygen as the main impurity.
